s1.syndrome_frame: Painful erosive skin lesion around a stoma site following abdominal surgery
salient_findings: Painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
Suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis on histopathology
Intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis on direct immunofluorescence
key_facts: Patient has a 10-year history of Crohn disease
Patient underwent total proctocolectomy and ileostomy
Symptoms developed 5 weeks after surgery
Lesion is painful and erosive
No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions are present
Microbiological cultures were negative
Histopathology showed epidermal erosion and suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3, histopathology showing suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Painful erosive lesion around stoma site, history of Crohn disease and recent surgery

shortlist.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1, epidermal erosion and suprabasal epidermal splitting

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Erosive lesion with histopathology showing epidermal erosion and suprabasal epidermal splitting

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Painful erosive lesion around stoma site, negative microbiological cultures and presence of autoantibodies

raw.rationale: The presence of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis, intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout the epidermis, and high levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 are characteristic of Pemphigus vulgaris.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: Typically associated with underlying neoplasms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
rejected.why: Characterized by autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 only, and typically involves the upper epidermis

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: Typically involves the basement membrane zone and has a different immunofluorescence pattern

rejected.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
rejected.why: Characterized by autoantibodies against type VII collagen, which is not mentioned in the vignette
